**Learning Path Table**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 3 | COU2279 | Cybersecurity Attack and Defense Fundamentals Specialization | Coursera | Expands on ethical hacking with a focus on attack and defense fundamentals. |
| 4 | COU467 | Pentesting Fundamentals for Beginners | Coursera | Introduces pentesting concepts, a key aspect of cybersecurity. |
| 5 | COU1294 | Security Principles | Coursera | Covers security principles, including risk, governance, and information assurance. |
| 6 | COU3000 | Security and Risk Management | Coursera | Develops risk management skills, essential for cybersecurity professionals. |

| 8 | COU4191 | Security Operations | Coursera | Introduces security operations, including asset management and cryptography. |
| 9 | COU532 | Security Infrastructure Management | Coursera | Covers security infrastructure management, including system security and security strategy. |
| 10 | COU2455 | SOAR for Enterprise Security | Coursera | Develops skills in security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR). |
| 11 | COU6423 | Tools for Security Specialists Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on tools and technologies used by security specialists. |
| 12 | COU247 | Web Hacker's Toolbox - Tools Used by Successful Hackers | Coursera | Introduces web hacking tools and techniques. |
| 13 | COU3642 | The Complete Pentesting and Privilege Escalation Course | Coursera | Develops advanced pentesting and privilege escalation skills. |
| 14 | COU1293 | Certified Ethical Hacking (v12) Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on advanced ethical hacking concepts and techniques. |
| 15 | COU1544 | Managing Linux Systems | Coursera | Introduces Linux system management, essential for cybersecurity professionals. |
| 16 | COU1619 | Kali Linux | Coursera | Develops skills in Kali Linux, a popular penetration testing platform. |
| 17 | COU3679 | Mandarin Chinese 3: Chinese for Beginners | Coursera | (Optional) Introduces Mandarin Chinese for those interested in international cybersecurity. |
| 18 | COU5521 | Learn to Speak Korean 1 | Coursera | (Optional) Introduces Korean language for those interested in international cybersecurity. |

**Learning Path Explanation**

This learning path starts with foundational knowledge of cybersecurity concepts, networking, and cloud computing (COU4667). It then builds on this knowledge with a comprehensive introduction to ethical hacking (COU3345), followed by a focus on attack and defense fundamentals (COU2279). The path then introduces pentesting concepts (COU467) and security principles (COU1294), before developing risk management skills (COU3000) and focusing on threat response (COU3447). The path continues with security operations (COU4191), security infrastructure management (COU532), and SOAR for enterprise security (COU2455). It then focuses on tools and technologies used by security specialists (COU6423) and introduces web hacking tools and techniques (COU247). The path develops advanced pentesting and privilege escalation skills (COU3642) and focuses on advanced ethical hacking concepts and techniques (COU1293). Finally, it introduces Linux system management (COU1544) and develops skills in Kali Linux (COU1619). This path covers the full duration requested and provides a comprehensive education in cybersecurity, network defense, and ethical hacking.

**Learning Path**

| 1 | COU89 | DevOps, Cloud, and Agile Foundations Specialization | Coursera | Builds on the DevOps prerequisite course, introducing cloud and agile concepts |
| 2 | COU2560 | AWS Cloud Technology Consultant Professional Certificate | Coursera | Focuses on AWS cloud technology, a key aspect of cloud computing infrastructure |
| 3 | COU3626 | DevOps Mastery Specialization | Coursera | Expands on DevOps knowledge, introducing key tools and technologies like Terraform and Kubernetes |
| 4 | COU625 | DevOps on AWS Specialization | Coursera | Applies DevOps knowledge to AWS, with a focus on continuous integration and delivery |
| 5 | COU1470 | Networking in Google Cloud: Fundamentals | Coursera | Introduces networking concepts in the context of cloud computing, a critical aspect of cloud infrastructure |
| 6 | COU2544 | Introduction to Terraform | Coursera | Focuses on infrastructure as code, a key aspect of cloud management and DevOps |
| 7 | COU5624 | Mastering Ansible Automation | Coursera | Expands on automation knowledge, introducing Ansible as a key tool for DevOps and cloud management |
| 8 | COU5655 | Introduction to High-Performance and Parallel Computing | Coursera | Introduces high-performance computing concepts, relevant to cloud infrastructure and DevOps |

**Path Explanation**

This learning path starts with foundational knowledge of DevOps and cloud computing, building gradually to more advanced topics. The first period focuses on DevOps prerequisites and cloud foundations, while the second period delves into AWS cloud technology. The third period expands on DevOps knowledge, introducing key tools and technologies. The fourth period applies DevOps knowledge to AWS, with a focus on continuous integration and delivery. The fifth period introduces networking concepts in the context of cloud computing, a critical aspect of cloud infrastructure. The sixth period focuses on infrastructure as code, a key aspect of cloud management and DevOps. The seventh period expands on automation knowledge, introducing Ansible as a key tool for DevOps and cloud management. Finally, the eighth period introduces high-performance computing concepts, relevant to cloud infrastructure and DevOps. This path covers the full duration requested, with at least one course per period, and provides a comprehensive learning experience in cloud computing infrastructure and DevOps deployment.

**Learning Path for Data Engineering with SQL and Spark**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 1-2 weeks | COU1795 | Data Engineering Foundations Specialization | Coursera | Foundational course covering data engineering basics, including ETL, Python programming, and relational database management systems. |
| 2-4 weeks | COU5253 | SQL for Data Science | Coursera | Introduces SQL concepts, essential for data engineering, and provides hands-on experience with SQLite. |
| 4-6 weeks | COU4368 | Introduction to Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Expands on data science concepts, including Python programming, cloud databases, and SQL, laying the groundwork for data engineering. |
| 6-8 weeks | COU1080 | Modern Big Data Analysis with SQL Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on big data analysis with SQL, covering data structures, file formats, and ETL processes. |
| 8-12 weeks | COU3513 | Engineering Data Ecosystems: Pipelines, ETL, Spark | Coursera | Covers data management, ETL workflows, and Spark basics, providing a solid understanding of data engineering pipelines. |
| 12-16 weeks | COU1763 | Microsoft Azure Databricks for Data Engineering | Coursera | Introduces Azure Databricks, a cloud-based platform for data engineering, and provides hands-on experience with data processing and management. |
| 16-20 weeks | COU3297 | Foundations for Big Data Analysis with SQL | Coursera | Focuses on big data analysis with SQL, covering data warehousing, database management systems, and data structures. |
| 20-24 weeks | COU6602 | Apache Spark with Scala – Hands-On with Big Data! | Coursera | Provides in-depth training on Apache Spark, including Spark SQL, DataFrames, and Datasets, essential for data engineering with big data. |
| 24-28 weeks | COU2286 | Introduction to Modern Data Engineering with Snowflake | Coursera | Introduces modern data engineering concepts, including data pipelines, data engineering, and Snowflake, a cloud-based data warehousing platform. |
| 28-32 weeks | COU4023 | Cloud Data Engineering | Coursera | Covers cloud data engineering, including machine learning, data science, big data, and distributed systems, providing a comprehensive understanding of data engineering in the cloud. |

This learning path starts with foundational courses in data engineering, SQL, and data science, gradually increasing in complexity and focus on data engineering with big data and cloud-based platforms. Each course builds on the previous one, providing a solid foundation for data engineering skills and preparing the learner for advanced topics in data engineering.

### How the path fits together

This learning path is designed to help the learner develop a solid understanding of financial accounting, from foundational concepts to advanced topics. The path starts with a basic introduction to accounting concepts (COU6515), followed by a more in-depth exploration of financial statements and the accounting equation (COU5281). The learner then develops their ability to read and analyze a company's financial statements (COU693), before expanding their knowledge to include advanced accounting topics (COU839). Finally, the learner applies their knowledge to real-world scenarios through a specialization in financial reporting (COU1803). This path provides a gradual increase in complexity, emphasizing application and development of analytical skills, and provides context for accounting concepts through the role of accounting in business decision-making.

This learning path is designed to help the learner become a better leader of a small technical team. It starts with foundational leadership skills, including team building, emotional intelligence, and systems thinking (COU4681). The learner then builds on these skills by learning about leadership dynamics, management, and team management (COU5641). The next course develops essential skills for leadership, teamwork, and negotiation, which are critical for a small technical team (COU3910). The learner then applies these skills in a hands-on way through the capstone course (COU4352). Finally, the learner focuses on leadership and organization design, which is essential for a small technical team (COU5842). This path is grounded in real-world scenarios and case studies, allowing the learner to see the relevance and application of new skills and knowledge in their own work context.

learning_path:
### Learning Path for a New Teacher

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU1101 | Learning to Teach Online | Coursera | Establishes foundational knowledge of online teaching and learning. |
| 2 | COU2472 | Online education: The foundations of online teaching | Coursera | Builds on the previous course, providing a deeper understanding of online education and teaching. |
| 3 | COU3731 | Online Learning Design for Educators Specialization | Coursera | Develops skills in designing online learning experiences, including lesson planning and virtual class management. |
| 4 | COU4487 | Get Interactive: Practical Teaching with Technology | Coursera | Focuses on interactive teaching methods, multimedia, and formative assessment, building on the previous course. |
| 5 | COU3488 | Teach English Now! Lesson Design and Assessment | Coursera | Applies the skills learned in the previous courses to lesson design and assessment, with a focus on English language teaching. |
| 6 | COU4311 | Innovative Teaching with ChatGPT | Coursera | Introduces the use of ChatGPT in teaching, emphasizing student engagement and personalized learning. |
| 7 | COU2202 | Conflict Resolution Skills | Coursera | Develops essential skills for managing conflicts and promoting positive relationships in the classroom. |
| 8 | COU2227 | Strategies for Teaching Perfect Tenses and Modals | Coursera | Focuses on teaching English grammar, including verb tenses and modal verbs, at an intermediate level. |
| 9 | COU5651 | Teacher SEL: Programs, Possibilities, and Contexts | Coursera | Explores social-emotional learning (SEL) and its application in teaching, at an advanced level. |

### Path Explanation

This learning path is designed to provide a comprehensive foundation in classroom teaching methods for a new teacher. It begins with foundational courses on online teaching and learning (COU1101 and COU2472), followed by courses that develop skills in designing online learning experiences (COU3731) and interactive teaching methods (COU4487). The path then applies these skills to lesson design and assessment (COU3488) and introduces the use of ChatGPT in teaching (COU4311). learning_path:
**Course Path for Project Management from Basics to Agile Delivery**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | EDX2192 | Project Management Life Cycle | edx | Foundational understanding of project management basics, including project life cycles, stakeholders, scope, time, cost, and quality management. |
| 2-4 weeks | EDX3248 | Agile Project Management | edx | Introduction to Agile Project Management, including its differences from traditional approaches, and the expertise to recognize the appropriate business conditions for the implementation of an Agile approach. |
| 4-6 weeks | EDX3326 | Advanced Project Management | edx | Building on the foundational understanding of project management, this course covers the skills to identify, define, and propose extensive project plans for suitable projects. |
| 6-8 weeks | EDX3342 | Strategic Project Management | edx | Moving beyond basic project management, this course applies strategic principles to effectively and successfully lead projects, including evaluating and selecting viable projects that are strategically aligned to business objectives. |
| 8-10 weeks | EDX3283 | Oxford Leading Strategic Projects Programme | edx | This course provides a set of personalized leadership skills to help guide teams through uncertainty to successful project delivery, including tools to manage potential project risks, capitalize on opportunities, and achieve organizational objectives. |
| 10-12 weeks | EDX3349 | Agile Leadership Principles and Practices | edx | Focusing on Agile leadership, this course covers the key roles, including Scrum Master, Product Owner, and Agile Team Member, and how to build self-organizing teams for Agile projects. |
| 12-14 weeks | EDX2440 | Portfolio Management, Governance, & the PMO | edx | This course covers the skills to explain what a PMO is and why it exists, describe how a PMO works within the broader organization, and identify and describe high-level strategies to set up, maintain, and wind down a PMO. |
| 14-16 weeks | EDX2447 | Persuasion and Presence for Program and Project Managers | edx | This course covers the skills to explain the rhetorical triad and its use in persuasion, establish a compelling and trustworthy presence (ethos), and create spoken and written messages with emotional impact to build understanding. |
| 16-18 weeks | EDX3323 | Product Management | edx | This course covers the tools to conduct a detailed analysis of the market to inform product strategy, use strategic planning to manage the development of a product, and create a concise marketing plan for the successful launch of a product. |
| 18-20 weeks | EDX3252 | Strategic Change Management | edx | This course covers the knowledge to create strategies for change with the ability to design initiatives that are impactful and sustainable throughout an organization, and practical skills to motivate for and implement change in a business, while overcoming stakeholder resistance. |
| 20-22 weeks | EDX813 | Risk Models for Project Managers: Monte Carlo and Beyond | edx | This course covers the skills to quantify and assess projects for budget, schedule, and return on investment, and how to develop a project budget estimate, model impacts on the project budget, and simulate using Monte Carlo methods the potential impacts of project risk on budgets and schedule. |

| 4 | COU3724 | International Law in Action: the Arbitration of International Disputes | Coursera | Delving into the practical application of international law, including arbitration and dispute settlement, in the context of international humanitarian law. |
| 5 | COU5529 | International Humanitarian Law in Theory and Practice | Coursera | Gaining a deeper understanding of international humanitarian law, its principles, and its application in real-world scenarios. |
| 6 | COU5181 | Climate Change and Human Rights | Coursera | Exploring the intersection of climate change, human rights, and international humanitarian law, with a focus on the impact of climate change on human rights. |

**Path Explanation**

This learning path begins with a foundational understanding of human rights principles and their application in open societies (COU3152). The next step is to understand the role of international institutions, including the United Nations, in promoting human rights and international humanitarian law (COU6411). The path then examines the intersection of human rights, healthcare, and international humanitarian law, with a focus on violence against healthcare workers (COU5028). The following course delves into the practical application of international law, including arbitration and dispute settlement, in the context of international humanitarian law (COU3724). The path then gains a deeper understanding of international humanitarian law, its principles, and its application in real-world scenarios (COU5529). Finally, the path explores the intersection of climate change, human rights, and international humanitarian law, with a focus on the impact of climate change on human rights (COU5181). This learning path covers the full duration of the learner's request, with at least one course per period, and prioritizes foundational understanding, gradual complexity, interdisciplinary connections, real-world applications, critical thinking and analysis, and emphasis on empathy and cultural sensitivity.

### Learning Path for a Better Leader of a Small Technical Team

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU4681 | Connected Leadership | Coursera | Foundational leadership skills, including team building and emotional intelligence. |
| 2 | COU5641 | Leading Teams | Coursera | Building on foundational skills, this course focuses on leadership dynamics and team management. |
| 3 | COU3910 | High Performance Collaboration: Leadership, Teamwork, and Negotiation | Coursera | Developing skills in negotiation, team management, and collaboration to lead high-performing teams. |
| 4 | COU4352 | Leading People and Teams Capstone | Coursera | Applying leadership skills in a real-world context, with a focus on team building and management. |
| 5 | COU5842 | Leadership & Organization Design | Coursera | Advanced leadership skills, including organizational design and change leadership. |
| 6 | COU1494 | Advanced Leadership Skills for the 21st Century Specialization | Coursera | Mastery of advanced leadership skills, including strategic leadership and leading a diverse workforce. |

### How the Path Fits Together

This learning path is designed to help the learner become a better leader of a small technical team. It starts with foundational leadership skills in Connected Leadership (COU4681), which provides a solid base for building on in Leading Teams (COU5641). The learner then develops skills in negotiation, team management, and collaboration in High Performance Collaboration: Leadership, Teamwork, and Negotiation (COU3910). The Leading People and Teams Capstone (COU4352) course applies these skills in a real-world context, and the learner then moves on to advanced leadership skills in Leadership & Organization Design (COU5842). Finally, the Advanced Leadership Skills for the 21st Century Specialization (COU1494) course provides mastery of advanced leadership skills, including strategic leadership and leading a diverse workforce. This path balances theoretical concepts with practical, hands-on exercises and real-world examples, and focuses on developing skills that are transferable across different contexts and situations.
